claim: Increasing communication volume, rounds, or token budgets alone does not consistently improve coordination outcomes in multi-agent LLM systems.
falsifier: Vary communication volume, rounds, and token budgets in multi-agent coordination tasks and measure success rates; the claim predicts that increasing these parameters will not consistently improve outcomes.

exclusions: limited to the reported coordination tasks and communication protocols; transfer beyond them is unestablished

title: Communication parameters–coordination outcomes principle

claim: Softmax activations are highly redundant during post-training across various pre-trained LLMs and datasets.
falsifier: Measure the redundancy (e.g., via cross-layer similarity or low-rank approximation) of Softmax activations in a pre-trained LLM during post-training.

exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported LLMs, datasets, and post-training settings; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Post-training process–Redundancy of Softmax activations principle

claim: Output-level metrics can indicate high unlearning success while internal representations retain substantial target knowledge, as revealed by activation-patching-based depth measurement.
falsifier: Apply an unlearning method, select its configuration using only output-level metrics, then measure internal erasure with an activation-patching-based metric; check for discrepancy.

conditions: unlearning method NPO with configuration selected without depth metric
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported model, unlearning method, and configuration; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Output-level metrics alone–undetected residual internal knowledge…

claim: For any NPO problem, the modified B̂ operator defined by adjacency between single-bit-differing feasible solutions is efficiently row-computable, and therefore e^{-iβ B̂} has an efficient quantum circuit.
falsifier: For a given NPO problem, construct B̂ as described, verify its row-computability, and check that the circuit depth for e^{-iβ B̂} scales polynomially in n.

conditions: B̂ is defined as adjacency matrix over feasible solutions differing in one bit with equal constraint value
the NPO problem is encoded with n bits
exclusions: limited to the reported construction of B̂ and the Aharonov–Ta-Shma method for row-computable sparse Hamiltonians

title: Quantum circuit implementing–existence of an efficient theorem
